items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: And Duke Ellington I was fortunate to hear when he still had his band with Johnny Hodges and Harry Carney.

ctx.x: Well yeah, I mean not them specifically. Basically how I got into listening to jazz was I guess through my older brother. I mean our parents had some 78s that belonged to I guess their parents. And it was a very mixed bag. But in it were some kind of interesting things. Nothing great, but I mean like there was something by “The Georgians” like this little combo from the 20s, and Bob Crosby’s Bobcats with Bob Haggart, which was really nice, great arrangement that he did, you know, some jazz things. And that just…

Beiderbecke Story on Columbia, which George Avakian did. So when I was 10, 11, 12, I was really absorbed in that. And pretty soon thereafter we were listening to Clifford Brown and Dizzy Gillespie. And one thing, this was in the late 50s — well early 60s I guess. One advantage that we had was that a lot of these people were still around then. So I could hear them. I only heard Louis once, but it was just a completely mind-altering experience. And Duke Ellington I was fortunate to hear when he still had his band…
So your parents must have been fairly supportive.
